title: The cupboard
rule: Shot as horror: creeping dread toward the cupboard, a shock cut to the hanging key, and the horror is the blank.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p77_the_cupboard.py (charcoal-card kit: charcoal99.py; key card and floor: p31_sounds_only.py; cut model: b1m2)
made: nine panels of articulated grey-card puppets and set pieces (charcoal99.pin_up: separate cut cards, charcoal rubbed in darker at the cut edges, drop shadows, brass split pins) from the b1m2 cut model, pinned on the teuf-teuf Cueva plain-rock wall (CC BY-SA 3.0, relief only) and printed through the teuf-teuf sepia ramp

horror lighting made per panel as one lamp pool with a deep falloff over the pinned cards (low key, vignettes, underlighting on the face at the glass and on his face), Dutch tilts on the clock and the shock panel

the creep: the memo under the lamp; his shadow (his own puppet blurred, enlarged and swung up the wall) going ahead of him to the cupboard; a pale face at the black glass; the emptied window still saying 'Much obliged!'; the cupboard looming as he reaches

the shock cut: the ANRC 1922 key cut as a pale card filling the big panel in the cupboard's black, the near leaf edge, a burst of rubbed charcoal strokes, CREEEAK in fattened charcoal pen lettering; SERVICE written on its tag
the blank: his underlit face with the forgetting line, then a small man at the open cupboard (key on its hook, SERVICE door shut) under a huge EMPTY cut-card thought balloon

captions as black cards lettered bone in the shared pen hand ('It was the simplest errand in the world.' ... 'Where the errand was: nothing.'); the four canon lines in the shared cut-paper balloons; folio '77 / The cupboard' (pen99.folio)

events.E0: P1 the memo under the lamp; P2 he rises, his shadow goes ahead
events.E1: P3 a face at the black glass: 'Pardon me — have you the right time?'
events.E2: P4 the clock, tilted, 4:10: 'Ten past four, by the clock.'
events.E4: P6 he reaches the cupboard; P7 shock cut: the key on its hook, tagged SERVICE
events.E5: P8 his face, pencil at chin: 'Well, here I am... and what for?'; P9 the empty thought balloon, key on its hook, SERVICE door shut

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

genre_cues: shadow going ahead of the figure
slow push-in on a looming door
shock cut with sound effect (CREEEAK) and burst lines
the empty thought balloon as the monster
beat: the push-in and the shock: the cupboard grows in three frames as he creeps up and reaches, a hard cut to the key in the dark (CREEEAK), his underlit face says the line, then the empty thought balloon swells over him in three frames
beat_frames: b03: the cupboard fills the frame, his hand reaches
b04: SHOCK CUT: the key in the black, CREEEAK
b05: his face, 'Well, here I am... and what for?'
b06: small man at the open cupboard, thought bubbles rising

self_check.outcome: key on its hook (P7, P9), SERVICE door shut (P9)
self_check.check: A reader names the genre as horror.
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
